# AI Was Supposed to Choose the Settings, but the Run Log Said “Not Provided”

After asking AI to handle a task, I checked the page showing its execution status. The model name was recorded, but the reasoning-effort field said “Not Provided.” I could not confirm what level of reasoning had been specified for the run.

The arrangement was supposed to be simple: the AI in the chat would choose that setting. I do not want to learn every technical option or manage it myself. Making those decisions is part of the work I want to hand over.

![Illustration of an AI assistant deciding settings and examining a run log](__KNO_ASSET__/assets/posts/en-ai-settings-not-provided-run-log/fig1.webp)

*Concept illustration of AI-selected settings and execution records, not a screenshot of the actual system.*

## Why Did the Log Say “Not Provided”?

I want AI to select a suitable model and reasoning level for each task. A routine job might not need an expensive or intensive configuration, while a more demanding job may require greater effort. If I have to decide this every time, I still have to learn and manage the settings I was trying to avoid.

In this case, I could see the model name in the execution record. What I could not find was a confirmed reasoning-effort value. That is why I challenged the “Not Provided” display: who was supposed to make the decision, and where did that decision go?

## The Display Did Not Explain What Had Gone Wrong

There were several possibilities. Perhaps no value had been selected in the first place. Perhaps the chat had selected one but it never reached the execution system, or perhaps the value was used but the status page failed to show it.

The record available at the time did not establish which explanation was correct. It established only that the model name was visible and the reasoning-effort value could not be verified.

I do not want to investigate those paths myself. I want the AI to examine the records, identify the cause, correct the mechanism if necessary, and verify the setting on a later run. That investigation and follow-through should also be delegated.

## Choosing a Lower-Cost Model Should Be AI's Job Too

In another workflow, I had already asked for routine email replies to use the lowest-cost model suitable for the job. Drafting a straightforward response and handling a complex technical problem do not always demand the same level of processing. Picking between them manually, over and over, is exactly the kind of management work I want to eliminate.

But the “Not Provided” label did not prove that an expensive model or reasoning level was actually used. To establish that, I would need reliable records of both the intended settings and the settings applied during execution.

## Three Things to Ask AI to Check

If you delegate tasks to an AI system, you can ask it to check the following rather than memorizing the configuration options yourself.

1. **Who chooses the settings?** Identify who is responsible for choosing the model and processing effort for each job.
2. **What actually ran?** Compare the intended configuration with the execution record, including any missing values.
3. **What happens when the record is incomplete?** Have the AI investigate the gap and verify the outcome after a correction.

Ask the AI to verify whether the settings it chose are reflected in the execution record.

## I Don't Want AI Management Handed Back to Me

For now, I was the person who spotted the missing information. That means some management work still lands on me, even though I had asked AI to take over the task.

I have not demonstrated a fully hands-off way of handling these checks yet. What I want is for AI to select the appropriate configuration, confirm what ran, and correct problems without making me inspect every status field.

Even the system that performs those checks is something I want AI to build and maintain.
